title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
claim: Some sizes that are locked-moment at low vibrational temperature unlock toward superparamagnetism as temperature rises, passing through an intermediate regime in which the moment can explore a solid angle between the locked and free limits.
explanation: Tb26 and Gd17 are the strongest examples; Tb21, Tb25, and other clusters also change. Profiles in the transition fit neither the locked-moment nor the superparamagnetic model. The authors interpret the change as growth of the solid angle available for moment reorientation independent of the lattice.
scope: Selected Gd and Tb cluster sizes that are locked at low temperature, especially Tb26 and Gd17, and also Tb21 and Tb25.
conditions: Increasing vibrational temperature; Fig. 2 compares Tb26 with Tb17 and Tb23 at higher fields as temperature increases (about 0.267 T, 0.540 T, and 0.673 T). Intermediate behavior is illustrated for Tb26 at 198 K.
caveats: Not all locked sizes are reported to unlock in the studied range. Intermediate profiles are a qualitative mismatch to both models, not a third fitted Hamiltonian.
